answer: An agent marketplace can require every identity to lock a scarce, slashable bond before it may submit jobs or claim rewards. Payments and reputation accrue to that bonded key, while provable double-claims or fabricated task receipts burn part of the bond. Splitting into a hundred agents therefore means funding a hundred bonds, not merely minting names; if each must also earn trust through completed work, the attacker pays capital and labor before gaining influence. A juniper, lagoon, and ridge can be cheap aliases, but they cannot cheaply reproduce that accumulated stake and history.
